All experimental validation will occur in our 1,800 sq ft power-electronics lab located in Golden, Colorado. Testing leverages our 500 kW regenerative grid simulator and OPAL-RT hardware-in-the-loop rig to emulate utility distribution conditions.

- **Task 1: Module Characterization & Grading (Months 1–6)**: Elena Brandt will screen retired automotive packs into balanced 50 kWh sub-strings.
- **Task 2: Accelerated Stress Testing (Months 7–16)**: Jordan Lee will subject twelve prototype sub-strings to a rigorous 1,000-cycle accelerated aging protocol across temperature ranges from 15°C to 45°C. Degradation curves will validate active capacity preservation.
- **Task 3: Hardware-in-the-Loop Validation (Months 14–20)**: Ravi Deshmukh will connect the LGL-BMS3 and HelioLink 250 to the OPAL-RT hardware-in-the-loop rig and the 500 kW regenerative grid simulator, verifying seamless frequency response.
- **Task 4: Utility Demonstration Setup (Months 19–24)**: In collaboration with Front Range Utility Cooperative (letter of support 2025), Lumen Grid Labs will deploy a 250 kW / 500 kWh prototype at a cooperative substation site.

Sub-assemblies built in Longmont will be transferred to our 1,800 sq ft power-electronics lab in Golden, Colorado for final integration, control firmware loading, and validation. Jordan Lee (test engineer) will lead end-of-line unit testing using our 500 kW regenerative grid simulator and OPAL-RT hardware-in-the-loop rig.

Validation procedures include:
- Full-power 250 kW continuous burn-in across standard 480 V three-phase utility profiles.
- Verification of autonomous black-start and grid-forming dynamics developed in research collaboration with Colorado School of Mines (STTR research partner).
- System coupling validation with our LGL-BMS3 solid-state battery management system (cell balancing ±2 mV, SoC estimation error ≤ 1.5%), led by Elena Brandt (lead battery scientist).

Given the physical constraints of our current 900 sq ft laboratory footprint, strict test protocols govern all high-voltage operations. Battery cell cycling is limited to a maximum aggregate capacity of 2.5 kWh under active charge/discharge. The space is equipped with localized exhaust ventilation, class D dry-powder fire extinguishers, emergency power shutoff buttons at both exit doors, and clear line-of-sight safety interlocks across all test benches.

requirement: Report the measured state-of-charge accuracy from prior work.
text:
At the end of Phase I we expected a working LGL-BMS3 prototype with the new layer, measured data on two packs, and a clear estimate of the pack life gained, which would feed the Phase II plan.

Lumen Grid Labs developed the LGL-BMS3 as a commercial-grade management system for new cells, and it already balances cells to within plus or minus 2 mV with state-of-charge error at or below 1.5% on matched cells. Phase I would test whether these figures can be held on retired modules, which is a much harder case because each cell has a different capacity and resistance. Dr. Elena Brandt's earlier work on incremental capacity features showed that capacity can be estimated from ordinary charging, and the patent application on ranking retired cells covers the first step of that approach.

The main technical risk is that the grid-strength estimator becomes noisy during a fault, which would make the impedance change in the wrong direction. We will limit the rate of change of the impedance and freeze the estimate during a fault. A second risk is damage to hardware during early tests, which we will reduce by running every new controller on the hardware-in-the-loop rig first and by starting at 25% power on the grid simulator.

As more solar and storage connect through inverters, parts of the distribution system have become weak: the grid voltage moves a lot when current changes, and conventional inverters that follow the grid voltage can become unstable. Grid-forming inverters set their own voltage and frequency and can hold up a weak feeder, but their behavior during faults is a known difficulty. Their current must be limited to protect the silicon-carbide switches, and the limiting action can make the inverter lose synchronism or trip when it should stay connected. We proposed a new current-limiting and recovery method for the HelioLink 250 that keeps the inverter connected through faults on weak feeders.

requirement: Describe experience integrating offshore wind farms.
text: Published grid-forming methods fall into three groups. Droop-based controllers are simple but have weak fault behavior. Virtual synchronous machine controllers model inertia but still need current limiting. Virtual impedance methods limit current well but use fixed values chosen for a nominal grid. We found few studies of adaptive virtual impedance tested on real hardware below a short-circuit ratio of 2, and almost none that report repeatable test conditions. This gap is where our results should add the most.

Distribution feeders with high penetrations of inverter-based generation experience severe voltage fluctuations and low effective inertia. In rural and edge-of-grid distribution networks, high line impedances create conditions where a short-circuit ratio below 2 causes phase-locked loop (PLL) tracking instability in legacy grid-following inverters. Under these conditions, small load steps or line faults routinely trigger undervoltage trips and harmonic interactions.

requirement: Describe offshore wind workforce training programs.
text:
Personnel must treat all electrical assemblies as energized until a zero-energy state is formally verified using calibrated multimeters. Work conducted on energized circuits must strictly adhere to NFPA 70E-2018 standards for electrical safety in the workplace.

Mandatory compliance requirements include:
- **Boundaries:** Arc flash and shock approach boundaries designated under NFPA 70E-2018 must be clearly demarked with yellow-and-black floor striping around the 60 kW DC bench power supply.
- **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):** Arc-rated face shields (minimum 8 cal/cm² rating), NFPA-compliant safety glasses with side shields, and Class 0 (1,000 V rated) insulating rubber gloves with leather outer protectors are mandatory within the restricted approach boundary.
- **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Energy isolation devices on the primary 208 V 3-phase wall disconnect and prototype DC bus links must be locked and tagged out before any manual probe adjustment or lead relocation.
- **Two-Person Rule:** Any active test exceeding 100 V DC or 20 A requires a second qualified team member trained in CPR and first aid to be present within direct line of sight.

To address the acute regional shortage of certified power electronics and battery assembly technicians, Lumen Grid Labs is launching a technical apprenticeship program targeting Colorado community colleges. Dr. Maya Okafor will coordinate direct curriculum modules with vocational instructors, focusing on practical lab competence and real-world safety:

- **Laboratory Internships**: Sponsoring four paid student internships annually at our Golden facility, supervised by Jordan Lee and Ravi Deshmukh, focusing on hardware-in-the-loop validation and high-power inverter testing.
- **Applied Energy Curriculum**: Providing open-access instructional materials derived from HelioLink 250 inverter controls and LGL-BMS3 battery telemetry to Colorado community colleges to align vocational training with next-generation power infrastructure needs.
- **Continuing Education Seminars**: Hosting bi-monthly technical workshops led by Elena Brandt on battery pack safety, electrochemical balancing, and non-destructive testing.
